messages.subject: Line types / legend
parts:
I'm trying to construct a graph comprised of overlayed density plots (data from >1 data.frame).
 
Hence, I want to use varying line types and colors to represent the density curves.
 
The desired line types and colors are represented as desired in the plot.  However, the corresponding line types are not displayed in the legend (i.e., diagnoal line in boxes are all solid).
 
This only seems to be only be a problem when I try to use more than 1 layer.
 
How do I get the proper line type displayed in the legend.
 
Thanks.
 
Marc

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Line types / legend
parts:
Also guessing without an example, but put the linetype specification
inside the aes() rather than outside it. Legends only get made for
things that are mapped, so that is why you would need to put it inside
the aes() (where the mappings are defined). You may also need a
scale_linetype_identity().

--

Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

messages.author: abfc91a3ea7fe477
messages.subject: RE: Line types / legend
parts:
Thank you to Brian Diggs and Joshua Wiley for previous advice on this.

Unfortunately, I still can't quite get the results I want.

I'd really like the key to reflect not only the line colors, but also line type. If I plot each density layer separately I get what I want, but not when I overlay them.

I've tried many ways to adjust the lines in the legend (e.g., put line specs in aes, use scale_linetype_manual, etc.), but might be overlooking something obvious...I'm relatively new to ggplot2.

This time I've included a little example. Made up data, but basically illustrates what I'm wanting to do with >=2 datasets.

Thanks.

Marc

d1 <- data.frame(x1=rnorm(10000,4,.75))
d2 <- data.frame(x2=rnorm(10000,3,.45))

library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot()
p + geom_density(data=d1, aes(x=x1, colour="Set 1"), linetype="solid") +
geom_density(data=d2, aes(x=x2, colour="Set 2"), linetype="dashed") +
scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,10), breaks=seq(0,10,.5)) +
labs(x="X-axis Label", y="Y-axis Label") +
scale_colour_manual(name="Data Source", values=c("purple", "black"))+
scale_linetype_manual(values=c("solid","dashed")) +
opts(title="Plot Title Here",
plot.title=theme_text(size=15,face="bold"),
panel.grid.minor=theme_blank(), panel.grid.major=theme_blank(),
panel.background=theme_blank(), axis.line=theme_segment(),
legend.key=theme_blank())

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: Line types / legend
parts:
Hi Marc,

Hopefully Hadley cleared things up, but just in case (if rather late):

d1 <- data.frame(x1=rnorm(100,4,.75))
d2 <- data.frame(x2=rnorm(100,3,.45))

library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot()
p + geom_density(data = d1, aes(x = x1, colour = "Set 1", linetype = "Set 1")) +
geom_density(data = d2, aes(x = x2, colour = "Set 2", linetype = "Set 2")) +

scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,10), breaks=seq(0,10,.5)) +
labs(x="X-axis Label", y="Y-axis Label") +

scale_colour_manual(name = "Data Source", values = c("Set 1" =
"purple", "Set 2" = "black"))+
scale_linetype_manual(name = "Data Source", values = c("Set 1" =
"solid", "Set 2" = "dashed")) +

opts(title="Plot Title Here",
plot.title=theme_text(size=15,face="bold"),
panel.grid.minor=theme_blank(), panel.grid.major=theme_blank(),
panel.background=theme_blank(), axis.line=theme_segment(),
legend.key=theme_blank())

Don't forget to include the name for both scales if you want a
simplified legend and put the linetype argument inside aes().

HTH,

Josh
